source: The saved read of the alpha3 hiring smoke (the served drafter, at f3e1a776): a costs-only model whose aim has no measure.
brief: Should I hire a Tech lead or two developers to increase productivity by at least 10%, while maintaining code quality? We have an urgent launch date in the next three months. We currently have six mid-weight developers, so we're lacking leadership. Our budget is £200,000, but we'd like to spend less.

canonical.question: Should you hire a Tech lead or two developers to increase productivity by at least 10% before the launch within three months, while maintaining code quality and staying within £200,000?

assumptions.text: The comparison counts each hire's total cost over the period covered by the stated budget; it does not assume the £200,000 is an annual or three-month budget.
assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: The option counts represent hiring commitments selected now, not an assumption that new hires are available or productive immediately.
assumptions.author: olumi

left_out.text: The 10% productivity target, the six-person mid-weight team, and the leadership gap are retained, but neither option's productivity gain is calculated.
left_out.why: Productivity needs a defined measure before additional delivery capacity and leadership support can be expressed in meaningful units without assuming that headcount equals output.
left_out.author: olumi

left_out.text: Meeting the launch date within three months is not yet calculated.
left_out.why: The required launch scope and remaining work are not specified.
left_out.author: olumi

left_out.text: Recruitment lead times and onboarding demands may materially reduce either option's contribution before launch.
left_out.why: No availability dates or onboarding arrangements were given, and no delivery calculation is yet defined.
